Decisions it builds on: ADR-001 (local admin console, static public site), ADR-002 (stack), ADR-003 (Accounts belong to Positions).\n\n## Problem Statement\n\nAWM at Kenyon runs a weekly Study Hall (Mondays 8–10pm, Hayes 311) and its Officers want members and curious students to be able to find out when and where it is and how to join.\n\nToday there is no site that members can reach. The old site exists only as local HTML files and was never put online. Changing it means editing raw HTML by hand, and the Study Hall time and place is written in three separate files, so a change has to be made three times. The Weekly email is therefore AWM's only form of communication, and a curious student who is not on the email list has nowhere to look.\n\nThe Officers change every year and each new Officer has a different level of computing experience. A site that needs HTML does not survive a Handover.\n\n## Solution\n\nA small CMS that the Officers use on one Co-VP's laptop, which produces the public AWM site.\n\n- An Officer signs in with their Position's Account, writes the Monday Study Hall reminder as a Post in plain text, and marks it Published. No HTML.\n- The standing Study Hall time and place lives in exactly one place: the Home Page. Home also shows the latest Published Post.\n- A Co-VP presses **Go live**, and the public site is updated. The Officer then sends the Weekly email by hand, with the same text plus the Post's Link.\n- The Co-VPs are Admins: they maintain the three Pages (Home, About, Join & Snacks), manage Accounts, and Go live. The Co-Presidents, Social Chair, and Treasurer are Editors: they write, publish, and delete Posts and edit the text of existing Pages. An Editor can never create, delete, or unpublish a Page.\n\n### Who uses it\n\n- **Visitors** (members and curious students) read the public site. They never sign in.\n- **Editors** (Co-President, Social Chair, Treasurer Accounts) post the Study Hall reminder and other news.\n- **Admins** (the Co-VP Account) run the site.\n\n### The seven required capabilities, in AWM's words\n\n1. **Login.** Each Position's Account signs in and out of the console. Passwords are stored as argon2 hashes.\n2. **Two roles.** Admin (Co-VP) and Editor (Co-President, Social Chair, Treasurer), with different permissions enforced in code.\n3. **Posts.** Officers create, read, update, and delete Posts: title, Link, Markdown body, Draft/Published, Author (a Position), and timestamps.\n4. **Pages.** Home, About, and Join & Snacks, with the same fields. Published Pages make up the public navigation.\n5. **Admin console.** A dashboard with counts and the Go live status, one content list that filters by status and type, and an editor with a preview.\n6. **Account management.** Admin only: create an Account for a Position, change its Role, set its password, and deactivate it. A Deactivated Account cannot sign in.\n7. **Public site and Go live.** Only Published content, sanitized Markdown, navigation built from Pages, and `cms publish` writing `site/` with relative paths. Go live is the button that runs it and pushes the result.\n\n## User Stories\n\n### Visitors\n\n1. As a curious student who is not on the email list, I want to see when and where Study Hall is on a public Home Page, so that I can show up without asking anyone.\n2. As a member, I want to see the latest Post in full on the Home Page, so that I know what is happening this week without needing the Weekly email.\n3. As a member, I want every Post to show its date with the weekday, so that I know which Monday \"tonight\" refers to.\n4. As a member, I want a Past posts list, so that I can find an older Post.\n5. As a member who clicked the Link in the Weekly email, I want to land on that exact Post, so that the email and the site agree.\n6. As a member, I want a Link from an earlier Weekly email to keep working, so that I never hit a dead page.\n7. As a curious student, I want an About Page describing AWM and its Officers, so that I know who runs it.\n8. As a curious student, I want a Join & Snacks Page with the Google Form link, so that I can join or request snacks.\n9. As a Visitor, I want the same navigation on every public page, so that I can move between Home, About, and Join & Snacks.\n10. As a Visitor, I want never to see a Draft, so that I only read what the Officers meant to publish.\n11. As a Visitor on a phone, I want the site to fit my screen, so that I can check the room on the way to Hayes.\n12. As a Visitor, I want Posts to read as coming from AWM with no individual name, so that it matches the Weekly email.\n\n### Signing in\n\n13. As an Officer, I want to sign in with my Position's Account, so that I can use the console.\n14. As an Officer, I want to sign out, so that the next Officer at the laptop does not act as my Position.\n15. As an Officer, I want to be signed out when the browser closes, so that a forgotten sign-out does not leave the Account open.\n16. As an Officer who mistypes, I want a clear \"wrong email or password\" message, so that I can try again.\n17. As a Co-VP, I want that message to be the same whether or not the Account exists, so that it gives nothing away.\n18. As a Co-VP, I want anyone who is not signed in to be sent to the sign-in screen, so that no console screen is visible without an Account.\n\n### Editors and Posts\n\n19. As a new Officer, I want to write the Study Hall reminder in a plain text box, so that I never have to learn HTML.\n20. As an Editor, I want a short hint under the text box showing how to make bold text and a link, so that I can add the Google Form link without looking anything up.\n21. As an Editor, I want to save a Post as a Draft, so that I can finish it later.\n22. As an Editor, I want to preview a Post before I publish it, so that I can see what Visitors will see.\n23. As an Editor, I want to mark a Post Published, so that it goes out at the next Go live.\n24. As an Editor, I want the Post's Link to be made for me from the date and title, so that I never have to type one.\n25. As an Editor, I want two reminders with the same title to get different Links, so that every week's Post has its own address.\n26. As an Editor, I want to fix a typo in a Published Post without its Link changing, so that the email link still works.\n27. As an Editor, I want to set a Post back to Draft, so that I can pull something published by mistake.\n28. As an Editor, I want to edit any Post, including one written by another Position, so that whoever is at the laptop can fix it.\n29. As an Editor, I want to delete any Post after an \"Are you sure?\" step, so that a cancelled or wrong Post can be removed.\n30. As an Editor, I want to post things other than the weekly reminder (a cancelled Study Hall, a snack update), so that all news goes through one kind of Post.\n31. As an Editor, I want a message after every save, publish, or delete saying what happened, so that I know it worked.\n32. As an Editor, I want to see the Post's public address once it is live, so that I can copy it into the Weekly email.\n\n### Editors and Pages\n\n33. As an Editor, I want to edit the text of an existing Page, so that I can update the Study Hall room or the Officer list.\n34. As a Co-VP, I want an Editor to be unable to create a Page, so that nobody adds to the navigation by accident.\n35. As a Co-VP, I want an Editor to be unable to delete a Page, so that the site's structure is safe.\n36. As a Co-VP, I want an Editor to be unable to change a Page's status, so that a Page cannot vanish from the navigation.\n37. As an Editor who types an Admin-only address directly, I want a clear \"no permission\" screen, so that I know it is not broken.\n\n### Co-VPs (Admins)\n\n38. As a Co-VP, I want to create a Page, so that the site can grow when AWM needs it to.\n39. As a Co-VP, I want to delete a Page other than Home after an \"Are you sure?\" step, so that I can remove one we no longer need.\n40. As a Co-VP, I want to set a Page to Draft or Published, so that I control what is in the navigation.\n41. As a Co-VP, I want Home to be impossible to delete or unpublish, so that the site always has a front page.\n42. As a Co-VP, I want to change the Study Hall time or room in one place, so that it is never out of date in a second file.\n43. As a Co-VP, I want a Go live button, so that I can update the public site without a terminal.\n44. As a Co-VP, I want the dashboard to show when the last Go live was, so that I know how current the public site is.\n45. As a Co-VP, I want a warning with the number of changes that are Not live yet, so that a Published reminder is never left unseen.\n46. As a Co-VP, I want a plain error if Go live fails, so that I know the public site did not change.\n47. As a Co-VP, I want Editors not to have the Go live button, so that going public stays with us.\n48. As a Co-VP, I want to see every Account with its Position, Role, and whether it is Deactivated, so that I know who can sign in.\n49. As a Co-VP, I want to create an Account for a new Position and choose its Role, so that a new Officer job can post.\n50. As a Co-VP, I want to change an Account's Role, so that a Position's permissions can change.\n51. As a Co-VP, I want to set a new password for any Account, so that a forgotten password or a Handover is a one-minute fix.\n52. As a Co-VP, I want to deactivate the Account of a vacant Position, so that it cannot sign in.\n53. As a Co-VP, I want to reactivate an Account, so that a Position that returns can post again.\n54. As a Co-VP, I want a Deactivated Account's Posts to stay on the site, so that history is not lost.\n55. As a Co-VP, I want the console to refuse to deactivate or demote the last active Admin, so that we cannot lock ourselves out.\n\n### Everyone in the console\n\n56. As an Officer, I want a dashboard with counts of Draft Posts, Published Posts, and Pages, so that I see the state of the site at a glance.\n57. As an Officer, I want one content list of Posts and Pages, newest first, so that I can find anything.\n58. As an Officer, I want to filter that list by Draft/Published and by Post/Page, so that I can find last week's reminder quickly.\n59. As an Officer, I want the list to show each Post's Author as a Position, so that I know which Position wrote it.\n60. As an Officer, I want the same navigation on every console screen, so that I never get lost.\n61. As an Officer on a phone-width window, I want console screens not to scroll sideways, so that they stay usable.\n\n### Running and grading\n\n62. As the developer, I want a seed command that creates the demo Accounts, the three Pages, and a few Posts (at least one Draft, one Published), so that the CMS can be used immediately from a clean clone.\n63. As the developer, I want `cms publish` and `cms deploy` to keep working from the terminal, so that the documented commands still work alongside the button.\n\n## Implementation Decisions\n\n### Modules\n\n- **Accounts and sessions.** Verifies a sign-in, hashes passwords with argon2, keeps the session in a signed cookie that ends when the browser closes, and exposes one guard for \"must be signed in\" and one for \"must be Admin\". All permission checks go through these guards, never through hidden links alone.\n- **Content.** One module that owns Posts and Pages: saving, status changes, Link generation, deletion, and the rules about who may do what. Routes ask it; they do not decide permissions themselves.\n- **Markdown rendering.** One function turns a Markdown body into sanitized HTML. The editor preview, the local public preview, and the export all call this same function, so nothing can be rendered unsanitized.\n- **Site export.** The existing export function is extended to write the whole public site from Published rows only.\n- **Go live.** Runs the export, pushes the result, and records the time. It is called by the dashboard button and by the `cms deploy` command.\n- **Admin console.** Dashboard, content list, editor, Accounts screen, sign-in screen. Server-rendered templates, no JavaScript framework (ADR-002).\n- **Seed script.** Extended to create demo Accounts, Pages, and Posts.\n\n### Data\n\n- **Account:** sign-in email (unique), display name (the Position, e.g. \"Social Chair\"), password hash, Role (`admin` or `editor`), active flag, created time.\n- **Post:** title, Link (unique among Posts), Markdown body, status (`draft` or `published`), Author (an Account), created time, updated time, first-published time.\n- **Page:** the same fields, plus a marker for which Page is Home.\n- **Site state:** the time of the last Go live, and a count of changes that are Not live yet.\n- Storage is SQLite (ADR-002). The database file is never committed.\n\n### Rules\n\n- **Roles.** Editors: create, edit, publish, unpublish, and delete any Post; edit the body of any existing Page. Admins: everything Editors can do, plus create and delete Pages, change a Page's title and status, manage Accounts, and Go live.\n- **Home.** Created automatically if missing. Cannot be deleted or set to Draft by anyone. Its body holds the standing Study Hall time and place.\n- **Links.** A Post's Link is the date plus a URL-safe form of the title (for example `2026-10-05-study-hall-tonight`). If that Link already exists, a number is added. A Page's Link is the URL-safe form of its title. A Link is set when the item is first Published and never changes after that, even if the title changes or the item goes back to Draft and is Published again. Officers never type a Link.\n- **Dates.** A Post's public date is its first-published time, shown with the weekday. Dates are shown in US Eastern time.\n- **Deleting.** Deleting a Post or Page is permanent and always goes through a confirmation screen. There is no trash.\n- **Accounts.** Accounts are deactivated, never deleted. A Deactivated Account cannot sign in, and an existing session for it stops working. The last active Admin cannot be deactivated or changed to Editor.\n- **Passwords.** Only an Admin sets a password, from the Accounts screen. No password is ever logged or shown.\n- **Not live yet.** Any change that would alter the public site adds one to the count: publishing or unpublishing, editing or deleting something Published. Edits to Drafts do not count. Go live resets the count to zero.\n- **Go live.** Admin only. If the push fails, the console shows a plain error, and the count and last Go live time are left as they were.\n\n### Contracts\n\n- Sign-in is a form posted to `/login` with fields `email` and `password`, matching the template's test helper. The console lives under `/admin`.\n- Every state-changing request is a POST carrying a CSRF token, including sign-out, delete, and Go live. A POST without a valid token is rejected.\n- An anonymous request to any console screen redirects to sign-in. A signed-in Editor requesting an Admin-only screen gets a 403 \"no permission\" screen.\n- Wrong email and wrong password give the same message.\n- `/` on the local app is a preview of the public site and shows Published content only.\n\n### Public site layout\n\n- Home at the site root; one file per other Published Page; one file per Published Post in a posts folder; a Past posts list in that folder; one stylesheet.\n- Navigation: Home first, then the other Published Pages in the order they were created, which gives Home, About, Join & Snacks. Past posts is linked from Home, not from the navigation.\n- Home shows its own body, then the latest Published Post in full. Past posts lists the older Published Posts, newest first.\n- Every `href` and `src` is relative. Files in the posts folder reach the stylesheet and the Pages with `../`.\n- No Author is shown publicly.\n- Raw HTML typed into a body is not passed through, and the rendered HTML is sanitized with an allowlist. Images are not in the allowlist.\n\n### Demo data\n\n- The seed creates four Accounts: Co-VP (Admin), and Co-President, Social Chair, and Treasurer (Editors). The Co-VP signs in as `admin@example.test` and the Social Chair as `editor@example.test`, matching the template's test helper; the other two use `copresident@example.test` and `treasurer@example.test`.\n- Passwords come from the environment. All three Editor Accounts use the one Editor demo password.\n- The seed creates Home, About, and Join & Snacks as Published Pages, and at least one Published and one Draft Post.\n\n### Screens\n\n- Every console screen has the same navigation and shows a success or error message after each action.\n- The editor has a formatting hint under the body box (bold, link) and a Preview button that shows the sanitized rendering.\n- Once a Post is live, the editor shows its full public address, built from the configured public site address.\n- No horizontal scrolling at 390 px on the public Home page or the console screens.\n\n## Testing Decisions\n\nA good test here drives the app the way an Officer or Visitor does and checks what they would see: a status code, a redirect, text on a screen, or a file in the exported site. Tests do not reach into the database or call internal functions to check how something was stored.\n\n### Seams\n\nThere are two seams, and both already exist in the template.\n\n1. **The console over HTTP.** Tests use the existing `client` and `client_as(\"admin\" | \"editor\")` fixtures to request screens and post forms. This covers sign-in, Roles, Posts, Pages, the dashboard, the content list, preview, Accounts, CSRF, and Go live.\n2. **The exported site.** Tests call the export into a temporary folder and read the files it wrote. This covers Published-only content, navigation, relative paths, sanitizing, dates, and Links.\n\nOne thing is replaced in tests: the push to GitHub inside Go live. Tests swap it for a fake that records it was called (or fails on purpose), so no test ever pushes to the real repository.\n\nEach test runs against its own temporary database seeded with the demo Accounts, so the fixed test passwords in the fixtures work.\n\n### What gets tested\n\n- Every row of `SECURITY-CHECKLIST.md` has at least one test.\n- Each Role rule has a test for the allowed case and the refused case, requested by direct URL rather than by clicking.\n- Draft content never appears in the export, the local preview, or the Past posts list.\n- A body containing `<script>` and an `onerror=` attribute is harmless in both the preview and the export.\n- Link rules: same-title collision, frozen after Published.\n- Last-Admin protection, Home protection, Deactivated sign-in refusal.\n- Not live yet count goes up on public-affecting changes and resets on Go live; a failed push leaves it unchanged.\n\n### Prior art\n\n`tests/test_t00.py` already uses both seams. Its four tests are kept. One must change when sign-in lands: it currently expects an anonymous request to `/admin` to return the \"hello admin\" page, which contradicts the rule that anonymous Visitors are redirected to sign-in. It becomes two assertions: anonymous is redirected, and a signed-in Officer sees the dashboard.\n\n## Out of Scope\n\n- Sending the Weekly email. This module stores\nAccounts, hashes passwords with argon2, verifies a sign-in, and exposes the\nguard routes use for \"must be signed in\". Passwords are never logged or stored\nin plain text.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport secrets\nimport sqlite3\nfrom contextlib import contextmanager\nfrom typing import Iterator\n\nfrom argon2 import PasswordHasher\nfrom argon2.exceptions import InvalidHashError, VerificationError\nfrom fastapi import Depends, HTTPException, Request\n\nfrom app import settings\n\n_hasher = PasswordHasher()\n# Verified against when the email is unknown, so both failures take similar time.\n_DUMMY_HASH = _hasher.hash(\"not-a-real-password\")\n\nSCHEMA = \"\"\"\ncreate table if not exists accounts (\n    id integer primary key,\n    email text not null unique,\n    display_name text not null,\n    password_hash text not null,\n    role text not null check (role in ('admin', 'editor')),\n    active integer not null default 1,\n    created_at text not null default (strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ', 'now'))\n)\n\"\"\"\n\n# Position, email, role, which demo password it uses.\nDEMO_ACCOUNTS = [\n    (\"Co-VP\", \"admin@example.test\", \"admin\", \"admin\"),\n    (\"Social Chair\", \"editor@example.test\", \"editor\", \"editor\"),\n    (\"Co-President\", \"copresident@example.test\", \"editor\", \"editor\"),\n    (\"Treasurer\", \"treasurer@example.test\", \"editor\", \"editor\"),\n]\n\n\n@contextmanager\ndef connect() -> Iterator[sqlite3.Connection]:\n    conn = sqlite3.connect(settings.DATABASE_PATH)\n    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row\n    try:\n        with conn:\n            yield conn\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\ndef init_db() -> None:\n    with connect() as conn:\n        conn.execute(SCHEMA)\n\n\ndef create_account(email: str, display_name: str, password: str, role: str) -> None:\n    with connect() as conn:\n        conn.execute(\n            \"insert into accounts (email, display_name, password_hash, role)\"\n            \" values (?, ?, ?, ?)\",\n            (email.strip().lower(), display_name, _hasher.hash(password), role))\n\n\ndef seed_demo_accounts(admin_password: str, editor_password: str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Create the four demo Accounts. Safe to run twice.\"\"\"\n    hashes = {\"admin\": _hasher.hash(admin_password),\n              \"editor\": _hasher.hash(editor_password)}\n    init_db()\n    with connect() as conn:\n        for display_name, email, role, pw_key in DEMO_ACCOUNTS:\n            exists = conn.execute(\"select 1 from accounts where email = ?\",\n                                  (email,)).fetchone()\n            if not exists:\n                conn.execute(\n                    \"insert into accounts (email, display_name, password_hash, role)\"\n                    \" values (?, ?, ?, ?)\",\n                    (email, display_name, hashes[pw_key], role))\n\n\ndef set_active(email: str, active: bool) -> None:\n    with connect() as conn:\n        conn.execute(\"update accounts set active = ? where email = ?\",\n                     (int(active), email))\n\n\ndef authenticate(email: str, password: str) -> sqlite3.Row | None:\n    \"\"\"Return the active Account for these credentials, or None.\"\"\"\n    with connect() as conn:\n        account = conn.execute(\"select * from accounts where email = ?\",\n                               (email.strip().lower(),)).fetchone()\n    stored = account[\"password_hash\"] if account else _DUMMY_HASH\n    try:\n        ok = _hasher.verify(stored, password)\n    except (VerificationError, InvalidHashError):\n        ok = False\n    return account if (ok and account and account[\"active\"]) else None\n\n\ndef get_account(account_id: int) -> sqlite3.Row | None:\n    with connect() as conn:\n        return conn.execute(\"select * from accounts where id = ? and active = 1\",\n                            (account_id,)).fetchone()\n\n\n# --- sessions and CSRF -----------------------------------------------------\n\ndef sign_in(request: Request, account: sqlite3.Row) -> None:\n    request.session.clear()  # new session on sign-in, with a fresh CSRF token\n    request.session[\"account_id\"] = account[\"id\"]\n    request.session[\"csrf\"] = secrets.token_urlsafe(32)\n\n\ndef sign_out(request: Request) -> None:\n    request.session.clear()\n\n\ndef csrf_token(request: Request) -> str:\n    token = request.session.get(\"csrf\")\n    if not token:\n        token = request.session[\"csrf\"] = secrets.token_urlsafe(32)\n    return token\n\n\nasync def require_csrf(request: Request) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Dependency for every state-changing route: reject a missing or bad token.\"\"\"\n    form = await request.form()\n    sent = str(form.get(\"csrf_token\", \"\"))\n    expected = request.session.get(\"csrf\", \"\")\n    if not expected or not secrets.compare_digest(sent, expected):\n        raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail=\"Invalid or missing CSRF token.\")\n\n\nclass NoPermission(Exception):\n    \"\"\"A signed-in Account asked for something its Role may not do.\"\"\"\n\n\ndef require_account(request: Request) -> sqlite3.Row:\n    \"\"\"Guard: must be signed in. Anonymous requests go to the sign-in screen.\"\"\"\n    account_id = request.session.get(\"account_id\")\n    account = get_account(account_id) if account_id else None\n    if account is None:\n        request.session.pop(\"account_id\", None)\n        raise HTTPException(status_code=303, headers={\"Location\": \"/login\"})\n    return account\n\n\ndef require_admin(account: sqlite3.Row = Depends(require_account)) -> sqlite3.Row:\n    \"\"\"Guard: must be an Admin.    return templates.TemplateResponse(\n        request, \"admin/login.html\",\n        {\"title\": settings.SITE_TITLE, \"home_path\": \"/\", \"error\": error,\n         \"csrf_token\": {\"title\": title, \"home_path\": \"/admin\",\n         \"csrf_token\": accounts.csrf_token(request),\n         \"flash\": request.session.pop(\"flash\", \"\"), **context})\n\n\n@router.get(\"\", counts=content.counts())\n\n\n@router.get(\"/content\", response_class=HTMLResponse, name=\"console_content\")\ndef content_list(request: Request, status: str = \"\", type: str = \"\"):\n    status = status if status in (\"draft\", \"published\") else \"\"\n    kind = type if type in (\"post\", \"page\") else \"\"\n    return render(request, \"admin/content.html\", \"Content\",\n                  items=content.list_items(status or None, kind or None),\n                  status=status, kind=kind)\n\"\"\"The FastAPI application.\n\nT00 (already done): the admin console answers at /admin and the public site\nanswers at /. That is the whole skeleton — it exists so you can prove the stack\nruns before you build anything on it.\n\nAdd your routes in their own modules (app/routes/posts.py and so on) and include\nthem here. Keep this file small.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException, Request\nfrom fastapi.responses import HTMLResponse, Response\nfrom starlette.middleware.sessions import SessionMiddleware\n\nfrom app import accounts, content, publish, settings\nfrom app.routes import auth, console, pages, posts\nfrom app.templating import templates\n\n\ndef create_app() -> FastAPI:\n    accounts.init_db()\n    content.init_db()\n    app = FastAPI(title=\"IPHS 400 MP2 CMS\")\n    # max_age=None: a session cookie with no Expires/Max-Age, so it ends when the\n    # browser closes.\n    app.add_middleware(SessionMiddleware, secret_key=settings.SECRET_KEY,\n                       session_cookie=\"session\", max_age=None,\n                       same_site=\"lax\", https_only=False)\n    app.include_router(auth.router)\n    app.include_router(console.router)\n    app.include_router(posts.router)\n    app.include_router(pages.router)\n\n    @app.exception_handler(accounts.NoPermission)\n    def no_permission(request: Request, exc: accounts.NoPermission):\n        return templates.TemplateResponse(\n            request, \"admin/no_permission.html\",\n            {\"title\": \"No permission\", \"home_path\": \"/admin\"}, status_code=403)\n\n    # The local preview of the public site: the same renderers the export uses,\n    # at the same relative paths, so it shows Published content only.\n    @app.get(\"/\", response_class=HTMLResponse)\n    def public_home():\n        return publish.render_front()\n\n    @app.get(\"/style.css\")\n    def public_css():\n        return Response(publish.CSS, media_type=\"text/css\")\n\n    @app.get(\"/{link}.html\", response_class=HTMLResponse)\n    def public_page(link: str):\n        page = publish.render_page(link)\n        if page is None:\n            raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=\"No such Page.\")\n        return page\n\n    @app.get(\"/posts/index.html\", response_class=HTMLResponse)\n    def public_past():\n        return publish.render_past()\n\n    @app.get(\"/posts/{link}.html\", response_class=HTMLResponse)\n    def public_post(link: str):\n        page = publish.render_post(link)\n        if page is None:\n            raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=\"No such Post.\")\n        return page\n\n    # Your ticket work plugs in here, e.g.\n    #   from app.routes import posts\n    #   app.include_router(posts.router)\n    return app\n\n\napp = create_app()\n\"\"\"The shared Jinja environment.\"\"\"\nfrom fastapi import Request\nfrom jinja2 import pass_context\nfrom fastapi.templating import Jinja2Templates\n\nfrom app import accounts, content, settings\n\n\ndef console_account(request: Request) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"The signed-in Account, so every console screen can show the same navigation.\"\"\"\n    account_id = request.session.get(\"account_id\") if \"session\" in request.scope else None\n    account = accounts.get_account(account_id) if account_id else None\n    # Passwords are never logged or stored\nin plain text.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport secrets\nimport sqlite3\nfrom contextlib import contextmanager\nfrom typing import Iterator\n\nfrom argon2 import PasswordHasher\nfrom argon2.exceptions import InvalidHashError, VerificationError\nfrom fastapi import Depends, HTTPException, Request\n\nfrom app import settings\n\n_hasher = PasswordHasher()\n# Verified against when the email is unknown, so both failures take similar time.\n_DUMMY_HASH = _hasher.hash(\"not-a-real-password\")\n\nSCHEMA = \"\"\"\ncreate table if not exists accounts (\n    id integer primary key,\n    email text not null unique,\n    display_name text not null,\n    password_hash text not null,\n    role text not null check (role in ('admin', 'editor')),\n    active integer not null default 1,\n    created_at text not null default (strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ', 'now'))\n)\n\"\"\"\n\n# Position, email, role, which demo password it uses.\nDEMO_ACCOUNTS = [\n    (\"Co-VP\", \"admin@example.test\", \"admin\", \"admin\"),\n    (\"Social Chair\", \"editor@example.test\", \"editor\", \"editor\"),\n    (\"Co-President\", \"copresident@example.test\", \"editor\", \"editor\"),\n    (\"Treasurer\", \"treasurer@example.test\", \"editor\", \"editor\"),\n]\n\n\n@contextmanager\ndef connect() -> Iterator[sqlite3.Connection]:\n    conn = sqlite3.connect(settings.DATABASE_PATH)\n    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row\n    try:\n        with conn:\n            yield conn\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\ndef init_db() -> None:\n    with connect() as conn:\n        conn.execute(SCHEMA)\n\n\ndef create_account(email: str, display_name: str, password: str, role: str) -> None:\n    with connect() as conn:\n        conn.execute(\n            \"insert into accounts (email, display_name, password_hash, role)\"\n            \" values (?, ?, ?, ?)\",\n            (email.strip().lower(), display_name, _hasher.hash(password), role))\n\n\ndef seed_demo_accounts(admin_password: str, editor_password: str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Create the four demo Accounts. Safe to run twice.\"\"\"\n    hashes = {\"admin\": _hasher.hash(admin_password),\n              \"editor\": _hasher.hash(editor_password)}\n    init_db()\n    with connect() as conn:\n        for display_name, email, role, pw_key in DEMO_ACCOUNTS:\n            exists = conn.execute(\"select 1 from accounts where email = ?\",\n                                  (email,)).fetchone()\n            if not exists:\n                conn.execute(\n                    \"insert into accounts (email, display_name, password_hash, role)\"\n                    \" values (?, ?, ?, ?)\",\n                    (email, display_name, hashes[pw_key], role))\n\n\ndef set_active(email: str, active: bool) -> None:\n    with connect() as conn:\n        conn.execute(\"update accounts set active = ? where email = ?\",\n                     (int(active), email))\n\n\ndef authenticate(email: str, password: str) -> sqlite3.Row | None:\n    \"\"\"Return the active Account for these credentials, or None.\"\"\"\n    with connect() as conn:\n        account = conn.execute(\"select * from accounts where email = ?\",\n                               (email.strip().lower(),)).fetchone()\n    stored = account[\"password_hash\"] if account else _DUMMY_HASH\n    try:\n        ok = _hasher.verify(stored, password)\n    except (VerificationError, InvalidHashError):\n        ok = False\n    return account if (ok and account and account[\"active\"]) else None\n\n\ndef get_account(account_id: int) -> sqlite3.Row | None:\n    with connect() as conn:\n        return conn.execute(\"select * from accounts where id = ? and active = 1\",\n                            (account_id,)).fetchone()\n\n\n# --- sessions and CSRF -----------------------------------------------------\n\ndef sign_in(request: Request, account: sqlite3.Row) -> None:\n    request.session.clear()  # new session on sign-in, with a fresh CSRF token\n    request.session[\"account_id\"] = account[\"id\"]\n    request.session[\"csrf\"] = secrets.token_urlsafe(32)\n\n\ndef sign_out(request: Request) -> None:\n    request.session.clear()\n\n\ndef csrf_token(request: Request) -> str:\n    token = request.session.get(\"csrf\")\n    if not token:\n        token = request.session[\"csrf\"] = secrets.token_urlsafe(32)\n    return token\n\n\nasync def require_csrf(request: Request) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Dependency for every state-changing route: reject a missing or bad token.\"\"\"\n    form = await request.form()\n    sent = str(form.get(\"csrf_token\", \"\"))\n    expected = request.session.get(\"csrf\", \"\")\n    if not expected or not secrets.compare_digest(sent, expected):\n        raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail=\"Invalid or missing CSRF token.\")\n\n\nclass NoPermission(Exception):\n    \"\"\"A signed-in Account asked for something its Role may not do.\"\"\"\n\n\ndef require_account(request: Request) -> sqlite3.Row:\n    \"\"\"Guard: must be signed in.    return templates.TemplateResponse(\n        request, \"admin/login.html\",\n        {\"title\": settings.SITE_TITLE, \"home_path\": \"/\", \"error\": error,\n         \"csrf_token\": accounts.csrf_token(request)},\n        status_code=status_code)\n\n\n@router.get(\"/login\", response_class=HTMLResponse)\ndef login_form(request: Request):\n    return {\"title\": title, \"home_path\": \"/admin\",\n         \"csrf_token\": accounts.csrf_token(request),\n         \"flash\": request.session.pop(\"flash\", \"\"), **context})\n\n\n@router.get(\"\", items=content.list_items(status or None, kind or None),\n                  status=status, kind=kind)\n\"\"\"The FastAPI application.\n\nT00 (already done): the admin console answers at /admin and the public site\nanswers at /. That is the whole skeleton — it exists so you can prove the stack\nruns before you build anything on it.\n\nAdd your routes in their own modules (app/routes/posts.py and so on) and include\nthem here. Keep this file small.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException, Request\nfrom fastapi.responses import HTMLResponse, Response\nfrom starlette.middleware.sessions import SessionMiddleware\n\nfrom app import accounts, content, publish, settings\nfrom app.routes import auth, console, pages, posts\nfrom app.templating import templates\n\n\ndef create_app() -> FastAPI:\n    accounts.init_db()\n    content.init_db()\n    app = FastAPI(title=\"IPHS 400 MP2 CMS\")\n    # max_age=None: a session cookie with no Expires/Max-Age, so it ends when the\n    # browser closes.\n    app.add_middleware(SessionMiddleware, secret_key=settings.SECRET_KEY,\n                       session_cookie=\"session\", max_age=None,\n                       same_site=\"lax\", https_only=False)\n    app.include_router(auth.router)\n    app.include_router(console.router)\n    app.include_router(posts.router)\n    app.include_router(pages.router)\n\n    @app.exception_handler(accounts.NoPermission)\n    def no_permission(request: Request, exc: accounts.NoPermission):\n        return templates.TemplateResponse(\n            request, \"admin/no_permission.html\",\n            {\"title\": \"No permission\", \"home_path\": \"/admin\"}, status_code=403)\n\n    # The local preview of the public site: the same renderers the export uses,\n    # at the same relative paths, so it shows Published content only.\n    @app.get(\"/\", response_class=HTMLResponse)\n    def public_home():\n        return publish.render_front()\n\n    @app.get(\"/style.css\")\n    def public_css():\n        return Response(publish.CSS, media_type=\"text/css\")\n\n    @app.get(\"/{link}.html\", response_class=HTMLResponse)\n    def public_page(link: str):\n        page = publish.render_page(link)\n        if page is None:\n            raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=\"No such Page.\")\n        return page\n\n    @app.get(\"/posts/index.html\", response_class=HTMLResponse)\n    def public_past():\n        return publish.render_past()\n\n    @app.get(\"/posts/{link}.html\", response_class=HTMLResponse)\n    def public_post(link: str):\n        page = publish.render_post(link)\n        if page is None:\n            raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=\"No such Post.\")\n        return page\n\n    # position in page.text and email in page.text\n    assert page.text.lower().count(\"deactivated\") >= 1\n    assert \"Admin\" in page.text and \"Editor\" in page.text\n\n\ndef test_accounts_screen_has_no_delete_control(client_as):\n    page = client_as(\"admin\").get(LIST).text.lower()\n    assert \"delete\" not in page\n    assert \"remove\" not in page\n\n\ndef test_every_accounts_form_carries_a_csrf_token(client_as):\n    page = client_as(\"admin\").get(LIST).text\n    forms = re.findall(r\"<form.*?</form>\", page, re.S)\n    assert len(forms) >= 5\n    for form in forms:\n        assert 'name=\"csrf_token\"' in form\n\n\ndef test_admin_sees_the_accounts_link_and_editor_does_not(client_as):\n    assert LIST in client_as(\"admin\").get(\"/admin\").text\n test_admin_creates_an_account_that_can_sign_in_with_an_argon2_hash(client_as):\n    response = create(client_as(\"admin\"))\n    assert response.status_code == 303\n    stored = db_rows(\"select password_hash, display_name, role from accounts\"\n                     \" where email = ?\", NEW[\"email\"])\n    assert stored and stored[0][0].startswith(\"$argon2\")\n    assert stored[0][1:] == (\"Webmaster\", \"editor\")\n    c, signed_in = sign_in_fresh(NEW[\"email\"], NEW[\"password\"])\n    assert signed_in.status_code == 303\n    assert \"Webmaster\" in c.get(\"/admin\").text\n\n\ndef test_a_duplicate_email_is_refused_with_a_message_and_creates_nothing(client_as):\n    admin = client_as(\"admin\")\n    response = create(admin, email=\"EDITOR@example.test\")\n    assert response.status_code == 400\n    assert \"already\" in response.text.lower()\n    assert db_rows(\"select count(*) from accounts\") == [(4,)]\n\n\ndef accounts\") == [(4,)]\n\n\ndef test_the_response_after_creating_shows_a_message_and_never_the_password(client_as):\n    admin = client_as(\"admin\")\n    response = create(admin)\n    assert NEW[\"password\"] not in response.text\n    page = admin.get(LIST)\n    assert \"Webmaster\" in page.text\n    assert 'role=\"status\"' in page.text\n    assert NEW[\"password\"] not in The user can send it another message and resume it, so the same task-id may notify more than once.</note>\n<result>I reviewed the uncommitted T06 changes: `app/accounts.py`, `app/main.py`, `templates/base.html`, and the new `app/routes/accounts.py` and `templates/admin/accounts.html`. This was a read-only review, so I ran nothing. There was no ReportFindings tool in this session, so the findings are below. I didn't spawn a further subagent, because this session is already the fresh one you asked for. The upstream range diff was empty, so the working tree is the whole scope.\n\nI found four real issues and nothing more that I'd stand behind. The guards (admin-only, CSRF, last-admin check, 404/400 handling) are otherwise correct.\n\n- `/home/msgre/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/app/accounts.py:107` (medium) — The last-admin guard in `set_role` and `deactivate` (line 129) is a check-then-act race. `_other_active_admins` and the `update` are separate statements, and Python's sqlite3 only opens a transaction at the first write. If two admins (A and B) each demote or deactivate the other at the same moment, both checks see an \"other\" admin and both updates commit. The system then has zero active admins and nobody can reach `/admin/accounts` to fix it. Fix by running `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` before the check, or by making the update conditional.\n- `/home/msgre/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/app/accounts.py:82` (low) — The duplicate-email check in `create_account` is check-then-insert. Two concurrent creates with the same email both pass it, and the second hits the unique constraint. The `IntegrityError` isn't caught, so the admin gets a 500 instead of the friendly 400. Catch `sqlite3.IntegrityError` and raise `AccountProblem`.\n- `/home/msgre/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/app/accounts.py:119` (low) — `set_password` doesn't invalidate sessions that already exist for that account. Sessions are signed cookies keyed only on `account_id`, and `require_account` doesn't compare against a password version. An attacker or former holder with a live session stays signed in after the Admin resets the password. Deactivation does cut the session off, because `get_account` filters on `active = 1`. Fix by storing a password-hash fingerprint or a session version in the session and checking it.\n- `/home/msgre/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/app/routes/accounts.py:69` (low) — `account_id: int` accepts values beyond SQLite's 64-bit range, such as `/admin/accounts/99999999999999999999/role`. The query then raises `OverflowError`, which gives a 500 instead of the \"No such Account\" 404. The same applies to the password, deactivate and reactivate routes. Bound the id with `Path(..., ge=1, le=2**63-1)` or catch `OverflowError` in `_target`.</result>\n<usage><subagent_tokens>46453</subagent_tokens><tool_uses>3</tool_uses><duration_ms>26666</duration_ms></usage>\n</task-notification>"}

Two Admins demoting or deactivating each other at the same moment could both pass the check and leave zero active Admins. | **Fixed.** Both now run `begin immediate` before the check, so the check and the update happen under one write lock. |\n| 2 | `app/accounts.py` `create_account` | low | A concurrent create with the same email would hit the unique constraint and give a 500 instead of the friendly 400. | **Fixed.** `sqlite3.IntegrityError` is caught and raised as the same \"already exists\" message. |\n| 3 | `app/accounts.py` `set_password` | low | Setting a password does not end sessions that are already signed in for that Account. {"parentUuid":"f0f00192-6bda-4b70-80de-f824136d9a6f","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-sonnet-5-5","id":"msg_011Cfdtt1RRPP58wCbJn8gXP","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Findings 1, 2 and 4 are fixed with a test each, and the commit is pushed to `main`. The full suite passes (201 tests).\n\n**The fixes**\n- **#1, last-Admin race:** `set_role` and `deactivate` in `app/accounts.py` now take the database write lock (`begin immediate`) before they count the other Admins. Two Admins acting at the same moment can no longer both pass the check. The test simulates the race (a competing write at the moment of the check) and fails if the lock is removed.\n- **#2, duplicate-email race:** `create_account` now turns the database's unique-email error into the same \"already exists\" message and a 400.\n- **#4, huge Account id:** an id too big for SQLite now returns 404 \"No such Account\" on all four id-based actions. Before, it returned a 500.\n- All three tests failed before their fix. I confirmed the lock test also fails when the lock line is removed.\n\n**Issue #7 comment:** it has a table of the four findings and how each was resolved. It also has your reasoning:\n- #1 is unlikely on a local laptop but cheap and protects the lockout case.\n- #2 and #4 were easy.\n- #3 was skipped because it's outside the ticket and risky to change sessions this close to Tuesday. I noted it as a possible follow-up ticket.\n\n**Commit:** `955c189` \"T06: Co-VPs manage Accounts\", with 6 files and `Closes #7` as the last line.\n- The commit has no `Co-Authored-By` trailer, even though the session's attribution reminder asked for one. Your `CLAUDE.md` says the message must end with `Closes #N`, and I took your rule over the reminder. {"parentUuid":"5e8b1a42-8431-4ec7-ada4-7f20851c52de","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"276f3e47-5bb3-49fd-8ea7-501dc16b1607","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":"<bash-stdout>title:\tT06 — Co-VPs manage Accounts\nstate:\tCLOSED\nauthor:\tmsgrespin\nlabels:\tready-for-agent, ticket\ncomments:\t1\nassignees:\t\nprojects:\t\nmilestone:\t\nissue-type:\t\nparent:\t\nsub-issues:\t\nsub-issues-completed:\t\nblocked-by:\tmsgrespin/iphs400-mp2-cms#2\nblocking:\t\nnumber:\t7\n--\n## Parent\n\n#1 (Spec: AWM at Kenyon CMS). Vocabulary follows `CONTEXT.md`.\n\n## What to build\n\nA Co-VP opens an Accounts screen that only Admins can reach. From it they see every Account, create one for a new Position, change an Account's Role, set a new password (for Handover or a forgotten password), and deactivate the Account of a vacant Position. A Deactivated Account cannot sign in. The console refuses to deactivate or demote the last active Admin, so AWM cannot lock itself out.\n\nAn Editor who types the Accounts address directly gets a \"no permission\" screen.\n\nThis is required capability 6 (User management) and the Account side of capability 2. It covers spec stories 37 and 48–55. Accounts are deactivated, never deleted, which is what keeps a Deactivated Account's Posts on the site.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] An Admin can open the Accounts screen, which lists every Account with its Position name, email, Role, and whether it is Deactivated.\n- [ ] An Admin can create an Account with a Position name, email, Role, and password. The new Account can sign in, and its stored password starts with `$argon2`.\n- [ ] Creating an Account with an email that already exists is refused with a message and no Account is created.\n- [ ] An Admin can change an Account's Role, and the change applies on that Account's next request: an Account changed to Admin can open the Accounts screen, and one changed to Editor gets 403.\n- [ ] An Admin can set a new password for any Account. The old password then fails, the new one works, and the password does not appear in any response.\n- [ ] An Admin can deactivate an Account. It then cannot sign in and gets the same generic message as a wrong password.\n- [ ] A session that was already signed in as an Account when it was Deactivated is redirected to sign-in on its next request.\n- [ ] An Admin can reactivate a Deactivated Account, and it can sign in again.\n- [ ] Deactivating an Account deletes nothing: afterwards it is still listed, marked Deactivated, with the same Position name, email, and Role.\n- [ ] The Accounts screen has no control for deleting an Account.\n- [ ] A request to deactivate the last active Admin, or change it to Editor, is refused with a message, and the Account stays an active Admin.\n- [ ] An Editor requesting the Accounts screen or any Accounts action by direct URL gets a 403 \"no permission\" screen and nothing changes. An anonymous request redirects to sign-in.\n- [ ] The console shows a link to the Accounts screen to an Admin and not to an Editor.\n- [ ] Every Accounts form carries a CSRF token and is rejected without one, and the response after each action shows a message.\n\n## Blocked by\n\nBlocked by #2 (T01)</bash-stdout><bash-stderr></bash-stderr>"},"uuid":"b56b5b22-d65e-4a2d-981d-981a2c3a6be3","timestamp":"2026-10-02T18:37:32.880Z","turnOrigin":"human","turnPosition":{"promptIndex":4,"turnIndex":5},"userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/msgre/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"6fcc16f5-b612-461c-a69a-c94aff9db888","version":"2.1.287","gitBranch":"main"}
